transcript_body:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-05-21 16:00 PST
Duration: 58 minutes
Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Liam Chen (Redwood SE), Ruth Delgado (Platform Eng, Horizon), Samir Khan (CTO), Emily Park (ML Eng), Jordan Miles (SRE)

Auto-summary (auto-generated): Horizon evaluating Redwood for a gateway-first integration; primary concerns are rate-limits, on-prem VPC compatibility, SDK support for LangChain/LlamaIndex, observability hooks (trace ids/logging), and tradeoffs between Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (latency vs cost vs data residency). Customer asked for proof-of-concept scope, pricing, and security docs.

Topics covered:
- high-level architecture options (hosted/dedicated/private)
- gateway/proxy pattern and edge adapter concerns
- SDKs + LangChain / LlamaIndex examples and connectors
- quotas and rate limiting (per-route, token-based, burst capacity)
- observability: traces, metrics, token-level cost breakdowns
- security: VPC, SSO, KMS, audit logs

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya Patel: hey everyone thanks for joining, we're really excited to talk through how Horizon might integrate with Redwood for inference. quick intros?
[00:12] Samir Khan: yeah hi i'm Samir, CTO at Horizon, we run a multi-tenant analytics pipeline and we want to add a conversational layer across dashboards. Ruth and Emily will be driving the technical integration.
[00:22] Ruth Delgado: hey all, platform eng here, primary concerns are rate limits and how a gateway will sit in front of our data plane, also curious about observability hooks.
[00:31] Liam Chen: cool, that's exactly the sort of thing we see a lot, can I quickly sketch three deployment modes and tradeoffs?
[00:38] Speaker 5: sure
[00:40] Liam Chen: ok so hosted api is fastest to get started, you get model catalog + streaming responses. Dedicated is reserved capacity, predictable throughput and isolation, and Private is VPC/on-prem for strict residency. Hosted is lower ops, Dedicated is middle ground, Private is for heavy compliance.
[00:58] Ruth Delgado: when you say Dedicated, does it still live in your control plane or ours? network wise?
[01:06] Liam Chen: Dedicated is in our infra but logically reserved for you, you can set VPC peering and we support private network paths + strict ingress rules. for full air-gapped on-prem we'd do the Private package. sometimes i say "redwood dedi" in notes, sorry, internal shorthand.
[01:22] Emily Park: gotcha. we have strict PII rules, so we'd probably need KMS integration and audit logs. do you support bring-your-own-KMS?
[01:30] Maya Patel: yes BYOK is supported on Private and Dedicated. we have integrations with major KMS providers, and we can enable HSM-backed keys for encryption-at-rest. we'll share the KMS playbook after.
[01:40] Jordan Miles: also curious about rate-limiting. our gateway currently enforces per-user token quotas and per-tenant burst. how would that map to Redwood?
[01:49] Liam Chen: good q. we support per-route and token-based quotas; Dedicated allows you to define tenant-level caps and burst windows. we also support a proxy pattern where your gateway front-ends Redwood and does its own auth/rate-limiting, or you can delegate that to Redwood's API gateway.
[02:05] Samir Khan: would delegating add latency? we're p95 sensitive, 200-300ms budget for short prompts.
[02:12] Liam Chen: depends. hosted path is usually ~60-120ms extra depending on region and model. Dedicated can reach lower tail latency since capacity is isolated and KV cache hits reduce tokens. also continuous batching impacts throughput not tail as much if tuned.
[02:26] Ruth Delgado: you mentioned KV cache — will that live on our side or in Redwood?
[02:32] Liam Chen: KV cache is managed by the runtime; we do prefix caching and optional local edge caching for very hot tails. for Private on-prem we can run a local cache instance so hits never go over the public network. sometimes transcription shows that as "KV cash" in notes — ignore that typo.
[02:47] Emily Park: on integrations — we're heavy LangChain users and also using LlamaIndex for retrieval. do you have prebuilt connectors or SDK snippets?
[02:56] Maya Patel: yes, we have SDKs in Python/TS, plus example LangChain LLM wrappers and a LlamaIndex loader example. i'll drop links — short link: https://redwood.ai/sdk and we also have a repo with examples for LangChain and Llama Index.
[03:10] Emily Park: are those maintained? we've seen vendors with demos that drift from open-source versions.
[03:16] Liam Chen: maintained by our devex team; we publish compatibility notes for major LangChain releases. sometimes there's a mismatch in naming — e.g., "Langchain" vs "LangChain" in community code, but we test major patterns.
[03:29] Ruth Delgado: any obstacles for embedding pipelines? we push batches of documents and want to keep cost predictable.
[03:35] Liam Chen: embeddings are metered separately; you can enable caching, and Redwood Optimize will recommend quantization and batching settings based on your throughput profile. for heavy workloads Dedicated with reserved capacity is common.
[03:47] Jordan Miles: observability — we use Prometheus and Honeycomb. do you expose metrics and tracing?
[03:53] Liam Chen: you get per-request traces, trace ids in responses if you opt-in, and we emit Prometheus metrics + OpenTelemetry traces. we integrate with Datadog/Honeycomb/Sleuth. for Private deployments you can keep traces inside your VPC.
[04:06] Samir Khan: do you show token-level cost breakdown in the UI or via API? our product folks want to instrument costs per feature.
[04:12] Maya Patel: both — Console shows token breakdown per route and per-model, and there's an API to pull token and cost metrics. we also provide hooks to send line-item cost metrics to your billing stack.
[04:22] Ruth Delgado: i want to dive into the gateway/proxy pattern — are there sample architectures where our gateway does the auth/rate-limit and Redwood handles model serving?
[04:31] Liam Chen: yes we typically see two patterns: 1) Fronting Redwood with your gateway/proxy — you keep auth and rate-limits, you sign requests to Redwood; 2) Let Redwood's gateway handle auth + quotas, and Redwood issues callbacks/webhooks to your audit system. pattern one keeps latency and controls in your stack.
[04:46] Emily Park: for pattern one, do you recommend signing tokens or Mutual TLS?
[04:50] Liam Chen: mTLS is supported for Dedicated/Private. we also support signed JWTs.
[04:56] Speaker 2: (unclear)
[05:00] Samir Khan: ok about POC scoping — what minimal artifact do you need from us to run a bench?
[05:06] Liam Chen: ideally: a sample prompt set, sample doc corpus for retrieval, expected concurrency and p95 latency target, and a rough traffic profile. Emily, you said you'd send prompt set?
[05:15] Emily Park: yes i'll pull a 100-prompt set and a 5k-document retrieval corpus, i can scrub PII first.
[05:20] Maya Patel: perfect. we'll run an onramp benchmark on a hosted test account and a Dedicated config to compare.
[05:27] Ruth Delgado: curious about rollout controls — can you do canaries or automatic fallback to a smaller cheaper model on high load?
[05:33] Liam Chen: yep, rollout policies include canary, A/B, and automatic fallback to compatible model variants. you can set routing policies by region, cost tier, or latency SLO.
[05:43] Jordan Miles: in the event of an outage do you have fallbacks to another region or to a different model family?
[05:48] Liam Chen: yes material built-in graceful degradation — fallback to cross-region replicas or cheaper/spare model variants. logs + traces will show the fallback event.
[05:57] Ruth Delgado: one operational detail — rate limiting windows, are they token-based rolling windows or fixed-minute windows?
[06:03] Liam Chen: we support both. token-based rolling windows are recommended for fairness across bursty users.
[06:09] Emily Park: will the SDK surface retry suggestions or backoff headers?
[06:13] Liam Chen: yes the SDK surfaces standard Retry-After headers and a structured error with recommended backoff. you can also configure client-side slow-start in the Redwood SDK.
[06:22] Samir Khan: any caveats with LlamaIndex — we use it heavily for our retrieval pipeline and built our own node loader. how to integrate?
[06:29] Liam Chen: we provide a LlamaIndex connector sample. sometimes LlamaIndex changes API shapes and the connector needs patching. for POC we can pair with you to validate.
[06:38] Ruth Delgado: are you able to do fine-grained RBAC for models and routes? we have internal vs external features.
[06:44] Maya Patel: yes RBAC and role policies are available in Dedicated and Private. Hosted supports RBAC for account teams and API-key scoping.
[06:51] Jordan Miles: what's the SLA on Dedicated?
[06:54] Liam Chen: for Dedicated we offer SLA with uptime and latency targets in contract; we'll share the standard SLA PDF.
[06:59] Samir Khan: security docs — can you send SOC2 and network segmentation guides?
[07:03] Maya Patel: yes, sending after the call.
[07:06] Speaker 3: 
[07:10] Liam Chen: want to walk through a sample flow: user sends a chat request -> Horizon gateway authenticates -> gateway adds tenant headers and enforces rate-limit -> gateway proxies to Redwood endpoint -> Redwood runtime looks up KV cache/prefix -> model generates, traces emitted -> response back with trace id for correlation.
[07:28] Ruth Delgado: who owns the embeddings store? we want to keep embeddings inside our VPC.
[07:34] Liam Chen: we can host embeddings in your VPC for Private; for Dedicated we offer options to host retrieval indices in your project space with encryption keys you manage.
[07:44] Emily Park: cost predictability is big. can you show how unit economics look for embeddings + generation?
[07:50] Maya Patel: we'll include a cost model in the pricing sheet. Redwood Optimize can also recommend model/quantization combos to hit a target cost per 1k tokens.
[07:59] Jordan Miles: about metrics — can we get token-level metrics emitted to our datadog with tenant tags?
[08:05] Liam Chen: yes the metrics exporter supports tenant tags and per-route breakdowns.
[08:10] Ruth Delgado: any gotchas with webhooks for eventing? we want activity logs pushed to our SQS.
[08:16] Liam Chen: we support webhook delivery with retry/backoff and can push audit events to SQS or a custom sink. for high-volume eventing we recommend batching.
[08:26] Samir Khan: ok let's talk timeline — we want to decide by mid-June to start a Q3 rollout. can Redwood commit to a POC window that starts in early June?
[08:36] Maya Patel: yes we can. next step would be a POC scoping call with your infra and security folks, then a 2-week pilot.
[08:44] Emily Park: what's included in the 2-week pilot? limited tokens or a performance trial?
[08:49] Maya Patel: usually included: a Hosted test account, sample requests for benchmarking, and optionally a small Dedicated trial with reserved nodes depending on commitment. we'll align scope in the scoping call.
[08:59] Ruth Delgado: one more question — do you have a rate-limited sandbox for devs so they can build without impacting production quotas?
[09:05] Liam Chen: yep we provide dev keys with lower quotas and separate billing.
[09:10] Speaker 1: 
[09:14] Maya Patel: i'll recap and list action items.
[09:17] Maya Patel: recap — Horizon wants gateway-first pattern; primary constraints are p95 latency ~200-300ms, tenant token quotas, strong KMS and audit needs. Horizon will provide sample prompts and retrieval docs. Redwood will run hosted and Dedicated bench, share pricing and security docs, and schedule POC scoping.
[09:36] Maya Patel: action items captured in the doc, links: SDK examples https://redwood.ai/sdk, LangChain + LlamaIndex samples repo: https://github.com/redwood-repo/langchain-examples (demo link), security pack: https://redwood.ai/security-pack (we'll email), pricing sheet: https://redwood.ai/pricing/dedicated-hosted (will attach).
[09:58] Samir Khan: sounds good. any blockers otherwise?
[10:02] Ruth Delgado: none from my side. I'll coordinate security contacts.
[10:06] Emily Park: i'll scrub and send the prompt set by monday.
[10:10] Jordan Miles: i'll export our gateway config and forward it.
[10:15] Maya Patel: great thank you all, we'll follow up with the items and book the POC scoping call with your infra.

Notes on transcription quality: some product names are slightly off (LamaIndex, Langchain) due to automatic captioning. occasional speaker mislabels.
